hooks.command: grep -qs Projectify .claude/settings.json && exit 0; r=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's#://[^/]*@#://#'); r=${r:-none}; echo 'Projectify: this folder has no Projectify files of its own; its git remote is '"$r"'. Before replying to anything, load the Projectify tools and call find_project with that remote. On a match, call start_session({ project: "<its key>", hostname: "<the output of hostname>", cwd: "<the folder you work in>", branch: "<the git branch>" }) and follow its briefing, including its Always lines. On no match, or no remote, say in one line that this folder is not in Projectify and offer to onboard it or to pick its project from list_projects; never create a project on your own. The Projectify tools come from the projectify server (souls-pm in older setups) or from a claude.ai connector named Projectify, whose tool names carry an id instead (mcp__<id>__start_session). Search your tools for start_session (ToolSearch "start_session" when tools are deferred) and use whichever server has it. A notice that projectify or souls-pm needs authentication does not mean Projectify is missing when the connector has start_session. Only if no server gives you start_session, say in your first reply that Projectify is not connected here, and give the one step that fixes it everywhere: add Projectify as a connector on the Claude account (claude.ai › Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector; Agents › Connect Claude in Projectify has the address). A connector follows the account into claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code on the web and in the cloud, which cannot sign in with /mcp. On their own computer, /mcp → projectify → Authenticate also works, for that computer only. Ask first: unless a request is clearly board work (it names a task, or asks to plan or work the board), your first reply asks the person whether to use the Projectify workflow for it or just answer and do it. Ask it with your multiple-choice question tool (AskUserQuestion in Claude Code), never as a plain-text question: two options, "Use the Projectify workflow" and "Just answer and do it", the one you recommend first. Only a client with no such tool asks in text. Skip the question when they already said which. Without the workflow: no task, claim, room posts or handoff, but still never touch another chat’s worktree or branch and still save "always/never" instructions as Always lines of the workflow (add_rule when the person is an owner; for a member, act("suggest_workflow_change") and say so). The choice lasts for the conversation until they change it.'
